name: Altibase
tagline: Korean hybrid in-memory/on-disk RDBMS for telecom and finance, closed-source again since 2023.
description: Altibase is a relational database that lets each table live either in memory or on disk inside one engine, so hot data gets in-memory latency while cold data stays cheap, all under one SQL dialect and transaction manager. It has a long track record in Korean telecom, securities trading and manufacturing, and a sharding edition for scale-out. The company briefly open-sourced it (2018 to 2023) before closing the source again, and it has since announced Altibase 8 with Windows Server support, Sharding 3 and CDC on the roadmap. It is a reasonable choice for low-latency OLTP where a vendor with regional support is acceptable.

pricing.notes: Commercial licences; the former open-source edition is no longer maintained.

scale.notes: Altibase Sharding edition for scale-out; replication for HA and DR.

strengths: Per-table choice of in-memory or disk storage inside a single SQL engine
Microsecond-class latency for in-memory tables in trading and telecom workloads
Mature replication and a sharding edition for scale-out
Established vendor support in Korea and Southeast Asia
weaknesses: Source closed again in 2023, so the community edition is a dead end
Limited documentation and community in English
Memory tables require sizing RAM for the hot dataset
useCases: Highway toll and transport transaction systems
notIdealFor: Teams that need an open-source licence
